featured.title: US–Iran Conflict Escalates
featured.content: The United States and Iran have returned to a heightened military confrontation, with fresh attacks reported on both sides. The escalation is increasing concerns about shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the effect on global energy supplies.

articles.title: BREAKING: US and Iran Exchange Fresh Attacks
articles.description: The United States and Iran exchanged attacks on Wednesday after a major escalation in the conflict. Reuters reports that the renewed fighting has put both countries back on a war footing and increased fears of a wider regional conflict.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran conflict Middle East military

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Becomes a Major Global Concern
articles.description: The continuing US–Iran conflict is threatening shipping through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reports that only a small number of commodity vessels transited the waterway on Tuesday, well below recent averages.

articles.title: Putin Says Russia Is Winning in Ukraine
articles.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia is making battlefield gains in Ukraine and criticised the current Ukrainian leadership as a negotiating partner. His comments indicate that major obstacles remain to diplomatic progress.

articles.title: Ukraine War Continues Despite Diplomatic Efforts
articles.description: The war between Russia and Ukraine remains active while diplomatic efforts involving the United States continue. Putin's latest comments suggest Moscow is maintaining a strong military position in its approach to negotiations.

articles.title: US–Iran Escalation Raises Regional Security Concerns
articles.description: Fresh US strikes and Iranian retaliation have increased concerns about the security of US forces, commercial shipping and energy infrastructure across the Middle East.

articles.title: US Markets Under Pressure From Oil and Rising Yields
articles.description: US financial markets entered September under pressure as rising oil prices and higher bond yields increased concerns about inflation and economic growth.

articles.title: Europe Watches Energy Risks as Oil Prices Rise
articles.description: European economies are closely monitoring the impact of higher oil prices and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Prolonged energy disruption could increase fuel and inflation pressures.

articles.title: Russia–Ukraine War Remains a Major European Security Challenge
articles.description: The continuing war in Ukraine remains one of Europe's major security concerns as Russia maintains its military campaign and diplomatic efforts struggle to achieve a breakthrough.

articles.title: Nigeria Labour Congress Rejects Petrol Price Increase
articles.description: The Nigeria Labour Congress has rejected the latest petrol price increase, warning that higher fuel costs could further increase transportation expenses and the cost of living. The union also questioned crude supply arrangements for domestic refineries.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economy Grows 4.43% in Q2 2026
articles.description: Nigeria's economy expanded by 4.43% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, up from 3.89% in the previous quarter, according to official data reported by Reuters. Growth improved in both oil and non-oil sectors.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economic Outlook Receives Positive Signal
articles.description: Moody's recently changed Nigeria's sovereign outlook from stable to positive while maintaining the country's B3 rating. The change reflects improved resilience to external pressures, although major fiscal and economic challenges remain.

articles.title: Nigeria Continues to Face Serious Security Challenges
articles.description: Kidnapping and attacks remain major security concerns in Nigeria. Authorities continue efforts to strengthen security operations and protect communities affected by armed groups.

articles.title: Oil Surges Above $95 as US–Iran Conflict Escalates
articles.description: Brent crude reached around $95.52 a barrel on Wednesday, while US West Texas Intermediate rose to around $91.02. Markets are increasingly concerned about disruption to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Global Markets Fall as Energy Risks Increase
articles.description: Asian stocks fell sharply as renewed US–Iran hostilities pushed oil prices higher and increased concerns about inflation, bond yields and global economic growth.

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Traffic Remains Severely Disrupted
articles.description: Only four commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to Reuters data. The reduced traffic is adding to concerns about energy supply and global shipping costs.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Alert: Job Seekers Targeted by Phishing
articles.description: Security researchers are warning users to remain cautious about unsolicited recruitment messages and links. Job seekers should verify recruiters and avoid sharing sensitive information through unexpected links.

articles.title: AI and Technology Remain Central to Global Investment
articles.description: Artificial intelligence, semiconductors and advanced computing remain major areas of investment as businesses and governments assess the economic impact of rapidly developing technology.

articles.title: Asian Markets React to US–Iran Escalation
articles.description: Asian markets came under pressure on Wednesday as investors reacted to higher oil prices, rising bond yields and renewed US–Iran military tensions.

articles.title: Oil Shock Creates New Pressure for Asian Economies
articles.description: Higher energy prices are increasing concerns about inflation and economic growth across Asia, particularly for economies dependent on imported energy.

articles.title: Africa Faces Potential Economic Impact From Strong El Niño
articles.description: Climate experts have warned that a potentially strong El Niño could create significant economic losses across parts of Africa through drought, flooding, food insecurity and other weather-related impacts.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: Security, energy and the economy dominate the global picture this morning. The United States and Iran have exchanged fresh attacks, increasing fears of a wider regional conflict. Brent crude has climbed above $95 as disruption around the Strait of Hormuz threatens global energy supplies. Asian markets have fallen under pressure from higher oil prices and bond yields. In Nigeria, the economy grew 4.43% year-on-year in Q2 2026, but the latest petrol price increase has triggered criticism from the Nigeria Labour Congress. The Russia–Ukraine war also remains active, with Vladimir Putin maintaining a hard line on negotiations.

bigQuestion: With wars pushing up energy prices and increasing pressure on economies around the world, can stronger international cooperation prevent today's crises from becoming a larger global economic shock?
